g.text: Reliable calls at scale: throughput, tail latency, timeouts, retries with backoff and
jitter, a retry budget, and a log and a trace of every call.
lessons/17-reliable-calls-at-scale/run.py (the prompts live here; the exercises ask
The story below is the setting. LANTERN is the local model; the case files are the text you send it.
Headquarters sends a synthetic batch to test the classifier before it goes to every force: invented
messages in the shape of real intercepts, with the right label on each. Forty thousand a month is the
figure. "Last time a system like this went live," Varma says, "it ran beautifully for an hour and then
the first error stopped the whole queue. Nobody noticed until morning."
She wants three numbers before anything is switched on: how many messages a minute LANTERN can sort, how
long the slowest ones take, and what happens when calls start to fail.
S00001 2026-10-11 16:52 Coach Ellis Leo lost a tooth today, call before bed.
S00002 2026-10-17 07:54 Payroll Your new badge is at reception, the old one stops working on
S00003 2026-10-12 12:00 Port authority Crew change for the Saltmarsh moved to Monday, paperwork
. Warm up, and choose the timeout
Timeout per attempt: 3s. Long enough that a healthy call is never cut off, short enough that a stuck one
does not hold a worker for minutes. config.yaml's 300s is for a cold 4B model on a CPU, not for a warm batch.
qwen3:0.6b, 300 messages per row, read back from .progress/calls.jsonl

The faults show in the tail, not the middle: the median message barely moved, the 95th percentile carries
the backoff waits and the cut-off stuck calls.

40,000 messages on claude-haiku-5-5, estimated from these token counts
Only successful calls reach the call log: a failed attempt never returns a reply. The runner's own log
events count the failures; the call log counts the work done.
1. In step 2, compare call p95 at concurrency 1 and 4. Where did the extra time go?
2. In step 3, compare the model call p95 with the whole message p95. What is in the gap?
3. In step 4, how many messages would you run again tomorrow, and how do you find them?

3. In run.py, set TIMEOUT to 0.05. What happens to healthy calls?

More detail: 'Try this' in lessons/17-reliable-calls-at-scale/README.md. Undo an edit with git checkout
<file>, or set every change aside with git stash.
On this machine LANTERN sorts about 1,158 messages a minute on qwen3:0.6b, with faults, so a month of
forty thousand is about 0.6 hours of work. Of 98 attempts made to fail on purpose, 0 messages were lost,
and the budget held an outage to 120 attempts. Every call is in the log with its prompt version, model,
The answers are another matter: 351 of 1,200 agree with the labels. Varma reads the log, not the
summary. "Every call, with its version and its time," she says. "Good. Hale will ask for exactly that.
And he will ask why we ran a model that is wrong most of the time. Before anything goes to court, we
prove the pipeline is right, not just that it runs."
